subsystems.name: Sensing element
subsystems.role: converts a physical quantity into a readable signal.
parts: MEMS pressure, temperature and humidity dies

subsystems.name: Node electronics and power
subsystems.role: lets one tiny device measure, store and transmit on its own.

subsystems.name: Communications and mesh
subsystems.role: moves data from huge numbers of tiny nodes to the internet.

subsystems.name: Localisation and timing
subsystems.role: gives every reading a place and a clock.

subsystems.name: Deployment platforms
subsystems.role: scatters nodes where people cannot go.

subsystems.name: Data backend
subsystems.role: turns an unmanageable stream into usable environmental fields.
parts: data assimilation into weather and climate models

subsystems.name: End-of-life handling
subsystems.role: prevents billions of devices becoming litter.

buildSteps.title: Choose the measurands
buildSteps.detail: Decide what the node must sense — temperature, pressure, humidity, particulate matter, specific gases — and design MEMS structures for those only, because every extra sensor costs power.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the dies
buildSteps.detail: Sensors and the microcontroller are patterned on silicon wafers by the same lithography used for computer chips, so a single wafer yields thousands of identical dies.

buildSteps.title: Solve the power budget
buildSteps.detail: Add a harvester and design the firmware to sleep almost always and wake briefly. Most nodes will transmit rarely and at very low power, since a tiny harvester produces at most milliwatts.

buildSteps.title: Design the link
buildSteps.detail: Use short-range radio, or backscatter that reflects an existing signal instead of generating one, and route packets through neighbouring nodes to a gateway.

buildSteps.title: Package it
buildSteps.detail: Encapsulate against water, salt, UV and pressure, or build the shell from biodegradable polymer and printed conductors so a lost node degrades on its own.

buildSteps.title: Mass-produce
buildSteps.detail: Drive unit cost to cents using wafer-scale fabrication and roll-to-roll printing for the disposable parts, otherwise the economics never work.

buildSteps.title: Distribute
buildSteps.detail: Release nodes from balloons, drones or aircraft along planned tracks, or attach them to existing buoys, masts and vehicles. Each node must stabilise and start reporting on its own.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate against references
buildSteps.detail: Cross-check every device against national metrology-grade stations, and correct for drift, ageing and contamination over time.

buildSteps.title: Assimilate the data
buildSteps.detail: Feed the stream into weather and climate models, which need careful weighting of millions of imperfect readings rather than raw addition.

prerequisites.why: phone-grade pressure, humidity and motion sensors already run on very little current.
ordinary radio transmitters need far more power than a tiny node can harvest; reflecting ambient signals works only over short distances.
a node the size of a grain has little area to catch sunlight or vibration, so lifetime is limited.

prerequisites.tech: Satellite backhaul for very small transmitters
prerequisites.why: small satellites can relay data from low-power ground nodes, but coverage and capacity are still limited.
scattering billions of devices into the environment is only acceptable if they break down safely or are retrieved.
today's models ingest thousands of observations; billions demand new statistical and computing methods.

pathway.milestone: established observing networks — radiosondes launched twice daily, thousands of drifting ocean profiling floats, ground air-quality stations, and orbiting Earth-observation satellites
pathway.unlocks: the models and data pipelines that any denser network would feed.

pathway.milestone: dense regional mesh deployments — smart-city air-quality grids, agricultural soil networks, instrumented rivers
pathway.unlocks: proving that cheap unattended nodes survive real weather and stay calibrated.

pathway.milestone: nodes cheap enough to be dropped and abandoned, with biodegradable casings
pathway.unlocks: coverage over oceans, forests and deserts where nobody can service a device.

pathway.milestone: a globally coordinated sensing layer feeding a single data system
pathway.unlocks: near-real-time environmental fields rather than interpolated maps — but only if disposal and radio spectrum are governed internationally.
